Foundations of Single-cell Data Science

This workshop introduces the basics of single-cell RNA sequencing (gene expression) and a minimal analysis workflow to an audience with a background in data science, machine learning, and statistics. The workshop is delivered as an installable R package, with a rendered html website, and Docker container. An emphasis will be placed on the how and why, not just the what, of each step.

Broad goals

  • Understand the structure of single-cell RNA-seq data.
  • Access the Bioconductor ecosystem.
  • Perform basic single-cell analysis.
  • Understand factors impacting analysis reliability.

This is

  • a crash course in the key steps of a single-cell RNA-seq analysis.
  • a discussion on how to approach new problems generally in DS.
  • considerations for effective analyses.

This isn’t

  • a deep dive of single-cell biology/immunology.
  • a demonstration of the only/best way to complete a single-cell analysis.

Installation

Rendered pkgdown website available here: https://michaelplynch.github.io/foundations-of-single-cell-data-science/

Option 1: Use Orchestra in your browser

You can run this workshop in your browser, with the required packages and data already installed. You will need a Google account.

  1. Go to Orchestra workshop templates and sign in with your Google account.
  2. Find Foundations of Data Science CRT Bioconductor Single-cell.
  3. Click Launch to start your session, or Connect if you already have a session running.

If you use Orchestra, you can skip the local installation and Docker instructions below.

Option 2: Install locally

The workshop can be installed locally using the below commands, from a fresh R session.


## Check R version
if (getRversion() < "4.6.0") stop("This workshop needs R 4.6.0 or later (you have ", getRversion(), "). Please update R and re-run.")

## install BiocManager
if (!require("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
  install.packages("BiocManager")

options(repos = BiocManager::repositories(version="3.23"))

## install remotes
install.packages(c('remotes','usethis'))

## install workshop package (takes care of dependencies)
remotes::install_github("michaelplynch/foundations-of-single-cell-data-science@1.0.1",dependencies=TRUE, upgrade='always')

## Course notebooks (same release); answer the prompts, notebooks are in vignettes/
usethis::use_course(
  "https://github.com/michaelplynch/foundations-of-single-cell-data-science/archive/refs/tags/1.0.1.zip",
  destdir = "~"
)

## Pre-download the dataset and check everything loads
sce <- TENxPBMCData::TENxPBMCData("pbmc4k")
#sce <- muscData::Kang18_8vs8()
pkgs <- c("SingleCellExperiment", "scater", "scrapper", "dittoSeq", "BiocStyle","UCell","mclust")
invisible(lapply(pkgs, library, character.only = TRUE))
BiocManager::valid()
message("Setup complete - see you at the workshop!")

Tested on Bioconductor 3.23 and R Version 4.6.x.

Option 3: Use Docker

Instead of installing packages locally, you can use the pre-built container. You’ll need Docker Desktop installed and running.

docker run --rm -p 8787:8787 -e PASSWORD=bioc ghcr.io/michaelplynch/foundations-of-single-cell-data-science:1.0.1

Then open http://localhost:8787 in your browser and log in with username rstudio and password bioc. The notebooks are in the vignettes/ folder.

  • Apple Silicon Macs (M1–M4): add --platform linux/amd64 after docker run.
  • The first run downloads several GB, so do it before the workshop.
  • Work is lost when the container stops.

Pre-requisites

  • Basic knowledge of R syntax
  • Basic machine learning and statistics
  • Previous data science/analysis experience

Useful resources

R

  • Orchestrating Single-cell Analysis (OSCA)
  • Orchestrating Spatial Transcriptomics Analysis (OSTA), a related and upcoming research area.

Python

  • Single-cell best practices

Participation

Interactive discussion on analysis strategy and results, follow-along coding, reflection on analysis strengths and limitations.

Data

Data used are from the 4k PBMCs from a Healthy Donor dataset released by 10x Genomics (2017), distributed via the TENxPBMCData Bioconductor package, and from Kang HM, et al. (2018). Multiplexed droplet single-cell RNA-sequencing using natural genetic variation. Nature Biotechnology 36:89–94. doi:10.1038/nbt.4042. PBMCs from 8 lupus patients, control and IFN-β stimulated, distributed via the muscData Bioconductor package.
